newsitem.title: UK: Digital move seen checking BSkyB growth.
newsitem.headline: Digital move seen checking BSkyB growth.

text.p: The launch of digital satellite services in 1998 will put a brake on BSkyB's profit growth although details of costs and revenue drivers are still sketchy, analysts said on Friday.
"What we have is a transition year in which they will essentially be supporting two technologies - analogue as well as digital," said Anthony de Larrinaga of brokers Panmure Gordon.
"We won't be looking for much in the way of growth. If they can get to 320 million (stg pre-tax profit) it won't be a bad performance in a transition year."

BSkyB had pre-tax profit of 314 million stg in the year to June 30 1997. Finance Director Richard Brooke told Reuters that the company endorsed the market view that operating profits were likely to be maintained in the current year. Operating profit totalled 374 million in the year just ended.
BSkyB shares were 33p lower at 437p at 1440 GMT, recovering from earlier lows of 428p.

Analysts noted that the 1996/97 pre-tax profit included a 14 million stg advance contribution on a programme supply deal and a 7.4 million stg write-back of a depreciation charge. Stripping out these elements, they said the underlying figure of 292.5 million was a little shy of market forecasts.

One analyst said that it was difficult to make forecasts for the current year without detailed information on digital marketing costs and before BSkyB had sealed deals to show pay per view movies and sport on its new service.
"Digital TV will become a major source of entertainment and Sky is in a strong position to be a, if not the, leading player," the analyst said.
BSkyB plans to launch its 200-channel digital satellite service next spring. Interactive services such as home shopping and banking will be launched a few months later.
Analysts said it would be interesting to see if BSkyB's churn rate -- the number of subscribers cancelling subscriptions -- rose when prices are increased next month.

They are also monitoring growth in analogue subscribers to see whether this tails off ahead of the digital launch. BSkyB said it added 43,000 "direct to home" subscribers in the last quarter, its best Q4 performance for three years.
